app.name: Utter
app.tagline: Your voice, turned into actions on your desktop.
theme.label: Theme
theme.desktopHint: Match your Matugen palette instead of the default grey and yellow.
theme.desktopMissing: No Matugen palette found for this theme.
language.label: Language
privacy.title: Completely offline
privacy.body: Your voice, your screen and everything you ask stay on your computer. Nothing is uploaded, ever.
privacy.fine: Utter only goes online when you download a model.
privacy.remoteBody: You've pointed {list} at a server outside your computer, so those requests leave it.
splash.promise: Private by design · runs entirely on your computer
states.configErrorBody: The settings file may be missing or damaged. Try again, or check the Troubleshooting page.
general.title: General
general.description: Start the assistant, choose how you talk to it, and make it yours.
general.hero.runningBody: Hold your assistant key and say what you want to do.
general.hero.stoppedBody: Start it to use voice commands. It only listens while you hold a key.
general.startup.title: Startup
general.startup.description: What happens when you log in.
general.startup.loginOn: The assistant starts automatically with your desktop.
general.startup.loginOff: You'll need to start the assistant yourself.
general.startup.loginMissing: The assistant service isn't installed yet.
general.trigger.title: How you talk to it
general.trigger.label: Listening method
general.sleep.title: Sleep mode
general.sleep.description: Free your graphics card when you're not using Utter. Hold either key to wake it.
general.sleep.enableHint: Say a trigger phrase in assistant mode to unload the AI models.
general.sleep.triggerHint: Say one exactly, e.g. “go to sleep”. Separate phrases with commas.
general.sleep.speechHint: Frees the most memory. Speech reloads in a fraction of a second on wake.
general.sleep.idleHint: Go to sleep by itself when you haven't used Utter for a while. Typing or clicking elsewhere doesn't count.
general.sleep.idleMinutesHint: Minutes without a push-to-talk key or a spoken command before Utter sleeps.
general.appearance.title: Appearance
general.appearance.description: Colours follow your desktop when a Matugen palette is available.
general.appearance.themeHint: Light, dark, or follow your system.
general.services.title: Background services
general.services.description: The pieces that run the assistant. Updated live.
general.serviceNames.runnerDesc: Runs plugins and enforces your safety rules
general.serviceNames.visionDesc: Finds things on screen from a screenshot
general.serviceNames.plannerDesc: Small AI model that plans multi-step actions
general.serviceNames.audioDesc: Applies your microphone and speaker choice
general.footer: Changes are saved straight away to {path}. Your comments in that file are kept.
apps.title: App actions
apps.description: What the assistant can do inside each app. Change a key combination if you've customised an app.
apps.pendingTitle: Your edits are saved, but not used yet
apps.pendingBody: Changes are stored in {path}. The assistant starts using them after its next update.
apps.listDescription: Common apps and your own. Click one to see and edit its actions, or switch to “All installed”.
apps.emptyBody: Try a different name, or clear the filter.
apps.editor.title: {name}
apps.editor.description: Say “{example}” and the assistant presses the matching keys in this app.
apps.editor.actionsHint: Each action is a key combination, like ctrl+t or alt+left.
apps.editor.searchUrlHint: Used for “search … in this app”. Must contain {q}.
apps.editor.noActions: This app has no key actions yet. Add one below.
voice.title: Voice
voice.description: The keys you hold to talk, how speech is recognised, and which microphone is used.
voice.keys.title: Push-to-talk keys
voice.keys.description: Hold a key, speak, then let go.
voice.keys.dictationHint: Types what you say into the focused field.
voice.keys.assistantHint: Turns what you say into an action.
voice.keys.escape: Press Esc to cancel. Modifier keys like Ctrl work too.
voice.keys.unmapped: That key can't be used ({code}). Try another one.
voice.stt.title: Speech recognition
voice.stt.description: Runs on your computer — your voice never leaves it.
voice.stt.engineHint: Faster-whisper is a good default on most machines.
voice.stt.modelHint: Bigger models are more accurate but slower.
voice.stt.languageHint: A code like en-GB or de-DE, or auto to follow your system language.
voice.stt.mismatch.title: This model only understands English
voice.stt.mismatch.body: Your spoken language is {language}, but {model} is an English-only model. Pick a multilingual model to switch to:
voice.stt.mismatch.downloadHint: The model is downloaded by your speech engine on first use; nothing is fetched until you choose.
voice.stt.deviceHint: Use your graphics card (CUDA) if you have one.
voice.mic.title: Microphone
voice.mic.description: Pick the microphone and check that it hears you.
voice.mic.noList: Couldn't list microphones, so your system default will be used.
voice.mic.levelIdle: Start the test and speak — the bar should move.
voice.tip.title: Try it
voice.tip.body: Click into any text field, hold your dictation key, say a sentence and let go.
voice.mac.description: The keys you hold to talk and how speech is recognised, using your Mac's own frameworks.
voice.mac.keysDescription: Hold a key, speak, then let go. Right ⌘ and Right ⌥ are good defaults because nothing else uses them alone.
voice.mac.escape: Press Esc to cancel. A single modifier such as Right ⌥ works best.
voice.mac.hotkeyBackendHint: Quartz is built in; pynput is a fallback if the event tap can't be created.
voice.mac.sttDescription: Apple's recogniser runs on the device; whisper.cpp is the offline fallback.
voice.mac.engineHint: Apple Speech needs no model download and is fast. whisper.cpp is more accurate for long sentences.
voice.mac.fallbackHint: Used when the first engine can't start, for example before Speech Recognition is granted.
voice.mac.localeHint: A locale such as en-US or es-ES with an on-device dictation model installed.
voice.mac.onDeviceHint: Never send audio to Apple's servers. Needs the language downloaded in Keyboard → Dictation.
voice.mac.modelHint: A whisper.cpp model name such as small.en, or a path to a ggml file.
voice.mac.deviceHint: Leave empty for the system default input, or paste a device name from Audio MIDI Setup.
voice.mac.tip: Click into any text field, hold Right ⌥, say a sentence and let go.
setup.title: Set up your Mac
setup.description: Utter needs a few permissions before it can listen, type and act. Grant them once; this page checks them live.
setup.linuxNote: On Linux the installer and systemd units handle setup. Nothing to do here.
setup.hero.title: A few permissions to go
setup.hero.body: macOS asks for each one the first time. If a prompt doesn't appear, open System Settings from the row and switch Utter on.
setup.hero.doneBody: Hold {assistant} and say what you want to do, or hold {dictation} to dictate into any text field.
setup.permissions.title: Permissions
setup.permissions.description: System Settings → Privacy & Security. Each one unlocks one thing.
setup.permissions.microphoneWhy: Hear you while a push-to-talk key is held. Nothing is recorded otherwise.
setup.permissions.speechWhy: Turn your voice into text with Apple's on-device recogniser.
setup.permissions.inputMonitoringWhy: Notice when you press and release the push-to-talk keys.
setup.permissions.accessibilityWhy: Type dictated text, press shortcuts and read the focused window's title.
setup.permissions.screenRecordingWhy: Take a screenshot only when an action has to find something on screen.
setup.runtime.sectionDescription: The assistant and its Python runtime live inside this app and are unpacked into your Library folder.
setup.runtime.title: Assistant runtime
setup.runtime.notInstalled: Not installed yet. This takes a few seconds.
setup.runtime.notBundled: This build has no bundled runtime; it uses the checkout at {repo}.
setup.agent.title: Background agents
setup.agent.description: Two small launchd agents run at login: the plugin runner and the voice assistant.
setup.agent.notInstalled: Not installed. Run macos/setup.sh from the Utter folder.
setup.note.process: Permissions are granted to utter (this app). The assistant runs inside it, so one grant covers the prompts, the background agent and this page.
setup.note.install: If a permission stays off after you switch it on, restart the assistant from the row above.
models.title: Models
models.description: The AI models stored on your computer. Download, check and remove them here.
models.installed.title: Installed
models.installed.emptyBody: The assistant still works with built-in rules. Add a recommended model below for smarter results.
models.installed.removeBody: {name} will be deleted from your computer. You can download it again later.
models.recommended.title: Recommended for your computer
models.recommended.description: Based on your processor, memory and graphics card. Nothing is installed without you.
models.recommended.zeroBody: Built-in rules, window info and accessibility always work — no download needed.
models.recommended.decisionApplied: Model name updated — match it to the name your server uses
models.pull.title: Add a model
models.pull.description: Downloads can be resumed and are checked for integrity.
models.pull.sourceHint: A Hugging Face repo (hf:org/name), a web link or a local file.
models.pull.needSource: Enter where to download from, like hf:org/name
models.pull.prefilled: Ready to download {name} — press Download to start.
models.storage.title: Storage
models.storage.description: How much space your models use.
models.storage.cleanupHint: Remove unfinished downloads and leftover files.
llm.title: AI model
llm.description: The AI that works out what you mean when no built-in shortcut matches.
llm.provider.title: AI server
llm.provider.description: Any OpenAI-compatible server, on your computer or elsewhere.
llm.provider.label: Server
llm.provider.urlHint: Where the server is listening, usually ending in /v1.
llm.provider.modelHint: The name your server uses for the model, e.g. qwen3-4b.
llm.behaviour.title: Behaviour
llm.behaviour.description: When the AI is asked, and how sure it must be.
llm.behaviour.fallbackHint: Only used when built-in rules and window info can't work it out.
llm.behaviour.head: Double-check actions
llm.behaviour.headHint: The AI picks from safe, prepared options. It can never invent its own commands.
llm.behaviour.thresholdHint: Higher means fewer mistakes but more “I'm not sure”.
tts.title: Spoken replies
tts.description: Let the assistant confirm what it did out loud. The voice runs on your computer.
tts.output.title: Voice output
tts.output.enableHint: Say a short confirmation when an action finishes.
tts.output.engineHint: Pick one that's installed, or install one with the link.
tts.output.voiceHint: An espeak voice like en-gb or de, or a Piper .onnx model. Empty derives it from the spoken language.
tts.output.languageHint: auto follows your system language. This is independent of the settings UI language.
tts.test.title: Try it
tts.test.defaultPhrase: Hi, I'm ready when you are.
tts.mac.description: Let the assistant confirm what it did out loud, with the voices built into macOS.
tts.mac.engineHint: say is the system voice command; AVSpeechSynthesizer uses the same voices in-process.
tts.mac.voiceHint: A voice name such as Samantha. Run `say -v ?` in Terminal to list them; empty uses the default.
tts.mac.rateHint: Words per minute. 0 keeps the system default.
perception.title: Screen
perception.description: How the assistant finds buttons and fields on your screen — and the rules that keep that safe.
perception.order.title: How it looks for things
perception.order.description: Cheapest and most reliable first. Screenshots are the last resort.
perception.order.t0Body: Which app and window are open.
perception.order.t1Body: Buttons and labels the app exposes.
perception.a11y.title: Accessibility
perception.a11y.description: Reads the labels apps expose, without taking screenshots.
perception.vision.title: Screen vision
perception.vision.description: Only used when nothing else can find what you asked for.
perception.vision.enableHint: Takes a screenshot and asks a vision model where to click.
perception.vision.widthHint: Smaller is faster. 1344 is a good balance.
perception.vision.gpuHint: Which GPU the vision server uses (0 is the first).
perception.trust.title: Why it's safe
perception.trust.description: What's on your screen can guide the assistant — it can never tell it what to do.
perception.trust.selectBody: Text from the screen, window titles or the clipboard can only pick between actions prepared in advance. It can never write a new command.
perception.trust.blockBody: If an action was built from screen content, the assistant refuses it before it runs.
perception.trust.orderBody: Vision is only tried after window info, accessibility and shortcuts.
plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.description: Add-ons that give the assistant its abilities, and the tools they rely on.
plugins.runner.title: Assistant core
plugins.runner.description: Versions agreed between the assistant and its plugins.
plugins.list.title: Installed plugins
plugins.list.description: Turning a plugin off takes effect after the assistant restarts.
plugins.list.offlineBody: Start it on the General page, then check again.
plugins.list.emptyBody: The assistant didn't report any plugins.
plugins.list.enabledToast: {name} turned on — restart the assistant to apply
plugins.list.disabledToast: {name} turned off — restart the assistant to apply
plugins.permissions.title: Permissions — {name}
plugins.permissions.description: Enforced permissions are blocked by the assistant. Advisory ones are a promise from the plugin.
plugins.permissions.none: This plugin doesn't ask for any permissions.
plugins.deps.title: System tools
plugins.deps.description: Programs the assistant uses. Missing ones have a link or a fix you can copy.
plugins.deps.emptyBody: The health check didn't report any tools.
plugins.deps.fixCopied: Command copied — paste it into a terminal
safety.title: Safety
safety.description: Decide what the assistant may do on its own. Risky abilities stay off unless you turn them on.
safety.banner.body: {list}. Turn them off when you don't need them.
safety.confirm.title: Ask before acting
safety.confirm.description: Important actions wait for you to say yes.
safety.confirm.enableHint: For example sending, deleting or buying.
safety.confirm.wordsHint: Words or phrases, separated by commas.
safety.risky.title: Risky abilities
safety.risky.description: Off by default. Your safety rules are always enforced by the assistant itself.
safety.risky.terminalHint: Types and runs commands in your terminal.
safety.risky.inputHint: Sends key presses and clicks to any app.
safety.risky.confirmBody: This lets the assistant do things that are hard to undo. Only turn it on if you understand the risk.
safety.limits.title: Limits
safety.limits.commandsHint: Leave empty to allow any command.
safety.limits.blockedHint: Requests containing these phrases are refused.
safety.tuning.title: Fine-tuning
safety.tuning.description: Small adjustments for how actions are performed.
safety.tuning.clickHint: How long each simulated click is held.
safety.targeting.title: App targeting
safety.targeting.description: Send typing or key presses to a specific app instead of wherever the cursor is. For example, “codex type ok” types into Codex even while you look elsewhere.
safety.targeting.modeHint: Round-trip focuses the app, acts, then returns. Stay leaves it focused. Off refuses targeted typing.
safety.targeting.restoreHint: After acting, return to the window you were using.
safety.targeting.timeoutHint: How long to wait for the target window to take focus. Advanced.
safety.targeting.macNote: On macOS, the assistant posts keys directly to the target app's process without changing focus. This is keyboard-only and experimental.
safety.targeting.otherNote: App targeting is available on Linux and experimental on macOS.
safety.targeting.wayland.title: Wayland
safety.targeting.wayland.description: With compositor animations on, targeting an app on another workspace briefly scrolls; turn animations off in your compositor for a near-instant switch.
safety.targeting.wayland.crossWorkspaceH: Whether targeting an app on another workspace is allowed.
safety.targeting.wayland.animationsOffHi: Lets automatic cross-workspace targeting skip the prompt.
diagnostics.title: Troubleshooting
diagnostics.description: Check the assistant's health, read its logs and create a report for bug reports.
diagnostics.health.title: Health check
diagnostics.health.description: Tests the assistant, its plugins and the tools it needs.
diagnostics.health.rawHint: The full JSON, for bug reports.
diagnostics.desktop.title: Desktop
diagnostics.desktop.description: Which compositor was detected and which backend drives windows, workspaces and screenshots.
diagnostics.desktop.unknownHint: Window actions are unavailable; dictation, typing and launching still work.
diagnostics.logs.title: Activity log
diagnostics.logs.description: What a background service is doing, live.
diagnostics.bundle.title: Support report
diagnostics.bundle.description: A zip with the health check, settings and recent logs.
diagnostics.bundle.exportHint: Saved to your Downloads folder, or your home folder if there isn't one.
about.title: About
about.description: Version, where things live, and credits.
about.tagline: A private voice assistant that runs on your computer.
about.runtime.title: On your computer
about.runtime.description: Where the app reads and writes.
about.appearance.title: Appearance
about.credits.title: Credits
